sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc=false][color=c2]Easy Mode[/color][/h2]
[center]If you would just like a short tl;dr rotation that will get you started right away, the one button rotation for Arcane is super bad, you will do a lot better using this simple talent loadout with the below easy mode rotation:[/center]
[center]
[dragonflight-talent-calc=blizzard/C4DAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAMzwYZmZmFMzQzMGAAAGAwMz0sssMDAEbAAsBzMDbWmxMLzYMzMzMswMzMzMAADAAwAMzAMAYYmZA heading=false]
[/center]
[h3 type=bar][color=c8]Easy Mode Priority Rotation[/color][/h3]
[color=c2]Opener:[/color]
When using [spell=44425], always aim to have 4 [spell=36032]s.
[ol]
[li][spell=365350][/li]
[li][spell=5143][/li]
[li][spell=44425] then [spell=321507] while its midair[/li]
[/ol][color=c2]Rotation:[/color][ol]
[li][spell=5143] if you have [spell=263725] and less than 12 [spell=384452].[/li]
[li][spell=44425] if [spell=451038] is active.[/li]
[li][spell=1295924].[/li]
[li][spell=44425] if you have [spell=263725] and 12 or more [spell=384452].[/li]
[li][spell=153626] if you have no [spell=36032]s.[/li]
[li][spell=30451].[/li]
[li][spell=44425] if you're out of mana.[/li]
[/ol][pad]
Below here you'll find a more in-depth presentation of the rotation, opener, and details on why we do what we do.
[/tab][/tabs]

[pad]

sections.heading: How to Play Arcane
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Arcane"][color=c8]Arcane Mage Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
These are the general principles Arcane operates on, feel free to scroll down a page to see the rotation details.
[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_arcane_arcane01 size=medium type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][icon name=spell_frost_manarecharge size=medium type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c2]Arcane Charges and Mana:[/color][/b] [spell=36032]s are generated by [spell=30451], [spell=1449], [spell=1243460], [spell=153626], [spell=321507], [spell=1295924], and lastly [spell= 5143] when talented into [spell=461248]. The only ways to clear them is [spell=44425], [spell=5143] with the talent [spell=461251] or waiting around while out of combat; spending charges with Barrage makes it hit harder and cleave more targets. Arcane Charges also increase the mana cost of Blast and its damage. Normally, this creates a loop where you want to use Barrage to reduce the mana spend at times so you can ensure you have mana when you want it, however that is not going to be relevant this season due to the reworks we received, [color=c8]Mana is not relevant[/color]. Try to have 4 Charges as much as possible for the best dps!
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][/td]
	[td][b][color=c2]The Proc Flow:[/color][/b]
        [/td]
	[/tr]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=spell_shadow_manaburn size=medium type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c8]Clearcasting:[/color][/b] [spell=263725] is our primary proc, it allows us to cast [spell=5143] which, among other things, provides [spell=384452] and provides solid single target and AOE dps via many strong talents.
        [/td]
	[/tr]

	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv12_ability_mage_arcanesalvo size=medium type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c8]Arcane Salvo:[/color][/b] [spell=384452] is fairly straight-forward, it stacks up and causes [spell=44425] to deal more damage, consuming the stacks. There are a lot of other ways that Salvo interacts with each hero talent tree and our spells and abilities and as such you should definitely spend the time to read those talents and understand the interactions as they will inform you on the why behind a lot of the rotation. Remember you can use the search function in the talent system to identify the talents that actually interact with Salvo!
	[/td][/tr]

	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=8026694 size=medium type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c8]Prismatic Bolt:[/color][/b] Our new Apex talent, [spell=1295924] is incredibly strong, it has a small % chance to proc when spending [spell=384452] with [spell=44425]. This can swing your dps quite a bit and because it does not stack so you really want to spend it quickly. The only higher priority is to get the 4pc tier set bonus [spell=1296930] to make Prismatic Bolt hit harder.[/td]
	[/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=ability_mage_arcanesurge size=medium type=round color=c8 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c2]Don't Sit on Cooldowns:[/color][/b] [spell=365350] gives us a huge refund on mana on top of the damage increase and other effects for the hero talents. The mana here isn't super important, but you want this damage, try to overlap it with vulnerabilities and add waves and other points of a fight where you need dps the most. it is almost always better to squeeze in as many as you can over the course of a fight or dungeon; that said, don't be afraid to volunteer to hold cooldowns for a specific problem in an encounter.
        [/td]
	[/tr]


[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]
[pad]

[h2 toc="Opener" type=bar][color=mage][icon name=ability_mage_arcanesurge type=round size=medium inline=true color=c8][/icon] Best Arcane Mage Opener[/color][/h2]
[pad]

[b][symbol=wow-atlas-quest-legendary-available] Please select a Hero Talent option to generate an Opener sequence[/b]
[/box]
[/center]
[/div]
[div display-options="SS|SF"]
[wrapper][center][box border=true][center]
[pad]
[div]

Remember that [spell=80353] is a group cooldown, you should always ask someone if you're not sure when this is best used for your group and coordinate with your teammates for optimal use. If you don't care about their opinions or you are solo, just use it whenever you think you'll make good use of it!
[pad]
A couple notes about cooldowns not part of any priority list in this guide, this is because they are terrible:
[ul][li][spell=205025] is used whenever you need Charges but do not have any other option but to use [spell=30451] at low Charges.[/li]
[li][spell=12051] is used when you run out of mana, but you really should never have this problem, and even if you did, you would likely run [spell=321526] instead.[/li]
[li]The opening [spell=44425] does not need 4 [spell=36032]s, you just want to get into your cooldown as soon as possible here.[/li][/ul]
[/div]
[pad]

[li]Cast [spell=5143] once, then [spell=44425].[/li]
[li]Cast [spell=321507] if either [spell=44425] and/or [spell=1295924] is mid-air [b]or[/b] [spell=365350] has 13 or less seconds remaining if its up.[/li]
[li]45-seconds later, when [spell=321507]s cooldown finishes, repeat the last step.[/li]

sections.body:
[h2 toc=false type=bar]Pre-Combat Check[/h2]
Before any combat happens, it is important for Arcane Mages to make sure the following steps are checked. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content, these are the things that keep you powerful, make a habit of just using them when out of combat all the time!
[center][wrapper width=800px][box]
[ul]

[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Cast Group Buffs -[/b] [color=q0]Use [spell=1459] to buff you and your party with additional Intellect, healers love you, Warlocks wish they were you, and melee fear you.[/color][/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Double Check Familiar -[/b] [color=q0][spell=205022] has a tendancy to wander off sometimes, double check that he's with you. To be serious, [spell=205022] despawns sometimes, even though [spell=1459] does not, so you have to pay extra attention to ensure you have it. Most buff tracking addons have something for this, including my UI export in this guide.[/color][/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Apply Your Barrier -[/b] [spell=235450] is insanely effective and having it up being combat just makes life easier and cost us nothing![/li]
[li icon=exclamation-circle][b]Is Aggro a Concern? -[/b] If you're at all concerned about aggro you should talent into [spell=55342] and use them before the pull. They don't do any damage but they make it so you generate 0 threat while they're active, allowing you to go crazy without upsetting your tank. This isn't worth doing though if you want to use them defensively.[/li]
[/ul]
[/box][/wrapper][/center]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=mage][icon name=ability_mage_arcanesurge type=round size=medium inline=true color=c8][/icon] Arcane Mage Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]

Arcane only has a few cooldowns, [spell=365350], [spell=321507], and [spell=12051]. Below are some considerations when using these:

[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Arcane Surge" icon=ability_mage_arcanesurge]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_mage_arcanesurge type=round size=medium inline=true color=c8][/icon][color=mage] Arcane Surge[/color][/h3]
[spell=365350] is simple, you use it, it spends all of your mana, does a burst of damage that hits 5 targets, then square root damage beyond that. [spell=365350] then buffs you for 15-seconds, granting 35% additional spell damage and 425% mana regen. There are other properties of this that come from hero talents.
[symbol=wow-hero-talent-spellslinger] [color=#e3a0eb]Spellslinger[/color]
Spellslinger changes [spell=365350] in one major way, [spell=443783] in Midnight causes your Surge hit to generate 8x [spell=443763]s and doubles Splinter generation during its buff; [spell=444968] also buffs Surge damage a decent chunk. Keep in mind that Splinters for Spellslinger are fuel for the fire, it's what makes Spellslinger work.
[symbol=wow-hero-talent-sunfury] [color=#f88a56]Sunfury[/color]
Sunfury has a few ways that it alters [spell=365350]. First, when you cast Surge, any [spell=448601] you have are consumed and added to your Surge buff for the duration of Surge. Second, when Surge ends, you gain [spell=451038] and [spell=1260272], enabling a powerful burst of damage, ultimately extending your burst window; there is also a talent that can extend Surge's window a couple seconds. Lastly, when you cast Surge, you spawn an [spell=448659], which cast empowered spells and the bird will also cast regular spells too. The bird is really complex in how it works, it detects whether it's single target or AOE and has a different action list based on this, it can cast it's own version of the following spells:
[ul]
[li][b]Empowered Abilities[/b][/li]
[li][spell=453326][/li]
[li][spell=450421][/li]
[li][spell=449569][/li]
[li][b]Single Target[/b][/li]
[li][spell=450500][/li]
[li][spell=450461][/li]
[li][spell=456139][/li]
[li][b]AOE[/b][/li]
[li][spell=456139][/li]
[li][spell=450462][/li]
[li][spell=450499][/li]
[/ul]
None of this is really important, it's just cool to know.
[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Touch of the Magi" icon=inv_ability_mage_radiantspark]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=inv_ability_mage_radiantspark type=round size=medium inline=true color=c8][/icon][color=mage] Touch of the Magi [/color][/h3]
[spell=321507] is a great nuke, but it has a few caveats in how to use it. First, Touch gives 4x [spell=36032]s meaning you can use it to quickly start full-power, sometimes, in easier content, it's better to fire and forget Touch just to get 4x Charges quickly for a quick [spell=44425]! Next, you want to ensure your target will live the entire length usually because  it does nearly all of its damage after the duration. Touch can be talented to cause a damage proc on direct damage via [spell=342231], proc a [spell=263725] via [spell=1243507], conjure [spell=443763] as [symbol=wow-hero-talent-spellslinger] [color=#e3a0eb]Spellslinger[/color], or, as [symbol=wow-hero-talent-sunfury] [color=#f88a56]Sunfury[/color], make [spell=44425] do more damage during Touch with [spell=449349]. After all these bolt-on effects, you also must consider that Touch's overall damage output is dependent on your ability to deal damage to your target during Touch's duration. Ultimately, this all adds up to a lot of damage investment over the 12-second period; you'll usually want to use it on the toughest enemy in the pack or the one most likely to kill the group if it doesn't die quickly!

All of that to say, this is a 45-second cooldown, don't sit on it more than a few seconds, especially the Touch that you're not pairing with [spell=365350].
[pad]
[/tab]
[tab name="Evocation" icon=spell_nature_purge]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=spell_nature_purge type=round size=medium inline=true color=c8][/icon][color=mage] Evocation [/color][/h3]
[spell=12051] is very straight forward, simply use it if you're out of mana and can't afford to cast another spell and have no other procs and it will restore all of your mana. Typically, you wouldn't bother with this if [spell=365350] is coming up shortly.
[pad]
[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Advanced Tips
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c8][icon name=Inv_artifact_tome01 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c8][/icon] Arcane Mage Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]
[pad]
These tips are more about being a good caster than anything, they're not all Arcane specific much less Mage specific. They have general applicability in World of Warcraft. [h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c8] Optimizing Damage as Arcane[/color][/h3]
Some key things to note in general about good gameplay that will make you stand out;
[ul]
[li]Optimize around [spell=384452]; try to think about your next few seconds of gameplay, will adds spawn that need to die fast? Will the adds that are up now die soon? Consider saving and not saving around the current conditions - more adds generally means more damage overall and to your main target, thanks to [spell=205028].[/li]
[li]Don't allow yourself to get frazzled with mechanics, when movement is required, try to react quickly and consider your [spell=212653] path and destination, ensure that you use Stutter Stepping in conjunction with Shimmer to minimize your downtime when handling mechanics.[/li]
[li][spell=235450] is a must-cast defensive. Mages are not as tanky as we used to be, and Barrier spells received a sizable buff to both their quality and to their cast time - they only require 0.5 seconds now to cast, so there's no excuse - you can't deal damage if you're dead![/li]
[li][spell=342245] is a strong defensive, but don't be afraid to also double tap it for mobility in the moment. This can help you keep up with classes that have much better sustained mobility.[/li]
[li]Your cooldown window only need about 17 seconds for [symbol=wow-hero-talent-spellslinger] [color=#e3a0eb]Spellslinger[/color] and a maximum of 23 seconds for [symbol=wow-hero-talent-sunfury] [color=#f88a56]Sunfury[/color] to deal their full damage, and 12s for your miniburns; don't hold your cooldowns for too long if you can help it, remember how short the cooldown on [spell=321507] and [spell=365350] are![/li]
[/ul]

[tab name="The Spellqueue Window" icon=spell_mage_nethertempest]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c8] The Spellqueue Window[/color][/h3]
There is a large amount of misinformation out in the internet about what the spellqueue window is and how it works. I hope this short write up will help elaborate on this misunderstood topic.

The spellqueue window is a brief window (default 0.4 seconds long) that exist at the end of casted spells and the global cooldown (GCD) that enables you to press your next button and queue the spell up at the exact point that your current cast or GCD finishes. This allows you to have seamless casting, see this example from one of my logs:
[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/guide/images/33126.png]
The [spell=30451]s begin exactly where the previous ones end. This minimizes downtime and without spellqueueing we would have gaps in our casting between spells; these gaps would add up overtime and result in significant losses, especially gaps during cooldown windows.

The above is not something people generally disagree with, the spellqueue window prevents gaps in casting, however, where some people make the misunderstanding is on how that specific window works. The mistaken recommendation is that people lower this window to some factor of their ping or as a response to queueing the wrong spell, most common are people lowering it to 0.1-0.2 seconds. The issue with this is that most people do not spam keys 5-10 times a second, which is what lowering the queue window to this point would require to maintain the same seamless benefit, while the 0.4 second default only requires 3 presses per second.

If this were the only issue and was solved by simply hitting buttons faster, I would say 'go for it' if you can sustain that during playtime, however, there is no benefit to lowering the window for the reasons above and so there is only risk here. The spellqueue window can be overwritten up until the spell that is queued begins; this means that lowering it because of ping or wrong spell queueing would be solved by simply just queueing the spell correctly as soon as possible. What is instead happening is that people are not queueing their spells, resulting in a gap of time where they then queue up the 'correct' feeling spell. The spellqueue window was added to the game to combat lag issues, the idea that people are trying to remove its value because of lag issues is comedy, and the people who will insist that it helps them not cast the wrong spells, especially during high haste, are just hitting the wrong buttons and breaking their queue to solve the issue rather than training themselves to hit the right button sooner.

Ultimately, this matters less for specializations that are resource starved or healers or tanks where the 'right' button press is often more important than uptime, it also matters less for the players at the top levels of gameplay, but it matters a lot for the vast majority of dps that we have seamless and consistent uptime. For this reason, I would highly recommend you leave this at the default 0.4 second value. I hope this explanation helps, but ultimately the real takeaway from this is that you should attempte to always have spells queued up properly for maximum uptime.

You can reset your spellqueue back to 400 with the code below, but be mindful that some addons will misguidedly set this lower for you.
[code]
/console SpellQueueWindow 400
[/code]

[color=c8]Tips:[/color]
- In single target it is a gain to cast at 20 Salvo, even if you don't have 4 Charges.
- You can cast Barrage with 19 stacks of Salvo if you have Orb Barrage talented.
- You can cast Barrage with 15 or more stacks of Salvo if you have Touch of the Magi is ready.

[tooltip name=Barr-SF]
[color=c8]Tips:[/color]
- You can cast Barrage with 8 or more stacks of Salvo if you have Touch of the Magi ready. Don't hold it!
[/tooltip]

[tooltip name=soul-SF]
[color=c8]Tips:[/color]
- For the best possible dps, don't Barrage the GCD before Soul starts!
[/tooltip]


[tooltip name=AM-SF]
[color=c8]Tips:[/color]
- The idea behind 12 Salvo here is really just that you'll typically Barrage, then Missiles, and unless you get very lucky, you'll Missile again. Remember you are reacting to HAVING 12 stacks, not trying to anticipate what you will have at the end of your channel.
- When you cast back to back Missiles, try to recast Missiles between the 2nd to last and last tick, the spell will refresh and you will still generate the same number of waves. This is known as Chaining.
